topic: Want to build your own home server with just a Android mobile
postText:
Turn your Android into a full-blown home server  

- I've been running a lightweight NAS on my old Pixel for the past 3 months, and it's handling 200 GB of backups without a hitch. The phone's ARM CPU and 4 GB RAM are more than enough for file sync and occasional transcoding. I also set up cron jobs to prune old logs, keeping storage tidy.  

- All you need is the phone, a USB-C OTG adapter, and a cheap SSD or HDD. I connected a 500 GB SSD via a powered hub; the power draw stayed under 5 W, so my home outlet never spikes. The SSD stays cool thanks to the phone’s built-in thermal management, no extra fans needed.  

- The magic happens in Termux: install proot-distro, pull Debian, and you have a full Linux environment. Add OpenSSH and Samba, and you can SSH from any device or mount the share on Windows/macOS. Because it runs in user space, you never have to root the device, preserving warranty.  

- Real-world use: I stream my movie collection to a Roku, host a personal Nextcloud instance, and even run a tiny Home Assistant hub-all from the same phone. The whole setup costs under $50 and runs on a single 5 V charger. I monitor uptime with a simple script that pings me if the service drops, and it’s never missed a beat.  

What would you run on a server that fits in your pocket?
